newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher on export sales report.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher on export sales report.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on bullish input from USDA's weekly export sales report, traders said.
"Corn exports were good. We were expecting 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
USDA Thursday said net export sales of U.S. corn during the week ended November 14 totaled 1.225 million tonnes, above trade expectations for 700,000 to 850,000 tonnes.
Bull spreading and net commercial buying contrilbuted to the advances with the action leading to ideas for light if any corn to be posted for delivery on the December contract.
First notice day for deliveries on the CBOT December is slated for Friday, November 29.
Rolling of positions also was mentioned.

"There's a lot of rolling of positions from the December into March, a lot of talk of maybe no deliveries and the export sales were good," said Paul Haugens of FIMAT Futures. But Haugens cautioned that the world supply of feedgrains remains adequate which should limit rallies in corn futures.
Corn closed 1/2 to 2-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with December up 2-1/2 at $2.72-1/2.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 70,000 contracts, below the 81,418 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, FIMAT Futures bought 600 May $2.80 calls at 11-3/4 cents, traders said. Term Commodities bought 400 March $2.60 puts and sold 200 March $2.80 calls at one cent.
Corn options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, below the 14,875 traded Wednesday.
